question: Why does Newport end each workday with a 'shutdown ritual'?
answer: To stop work properly so the mind can rest. He reviews his tasks, plans the next day, then says a set phrase: 'Schedule shutdown, complete.' Newport cites research suggesting that unfinished tasks nag at the mind until there is a plan for them, so a clear plan lets evenings bring real recovery.
move: End work with a plan, so unfinished tasks stop nagging you.
simply: At the end of the day Newport checks his list, plans tomorrow and says 'shutdown complete'. Then his brain can let work go.
why: Rest is what makes the next day's focus possible. A two-minute ritual can stop work from leaking into your evening.
